Maybe the reason we don't see or hear about time travelers from the future is because the human race is gone before we discover worm holes (or how to get to them).

Or, any attempt at time travel results in an alternate reality where time travel was successful and we just continue on as if nothing has happened.

Think about it.

Person A is 30 years old, they travel back in time to meet their 10 year old self. Now there is a point in the past where a 10 and 30 year old Person A existed, which did not happen before. A new reality is created, one in which Person A travelled back in time.

Person A tries to travel back to the date from which he departed originally. He ends up in a future where there is already a 30 year old Person A, the now adult version of the 10 year old Person A from the "past".

The first Person A is from an alternate time line, in which his 10 year old self never met his older counterpart, as he had not time travelled yet. The Universe therein avoids the paradox, and time travel is possible.

Everything is perspective. If you travel back in time, you do, but only for yourself. Noone else acknowledges that you have traveled back in time, only people from your perspective see and understand that.

This is why the "I'm going to travel back in time and kill my enemy" trope is shit, because if you do that you're not killing your enemy you're removing yourself from his timeline and moving to a timeline where he doesn't exist.

If anything you might be able to get him to help you.

My theory on time travel has been like this for a while, actually. (visualization)

Unfortunately for all your theories, this all relies on one fact: an infinite many timelines with nearly an infinite amount of information must exist for this to work. If you cannot include that in your theory or do not believe it, then how on earth did you expect it to work?

Maybe time travel is possible but not in combination with travel in space. So you go back in time, but the earth has moved further around the sun, the solar system has moved within the Milkyway, the galaxy has moved closer to Andromeda,...

This is often why Science Fiction involving time travel mentions time and spacial coordinates. You'd need to not only know your position in time, but space as well, as relates to that moment in time.

Perhaps we haven't figured out that last part yet and there are many dead time travellers orbiting the galaxy. Poor bastards.
